root_cause: The Phase 84 request reached a healthy Security API over a fully validated TLS session but carried NO identity at all - no admin TLS client certificate and no credentials - and the cluster has anonymous authentication disabled (plugins.security.anonymous_auth_enabled=false) with the Security API restricted to plugins.security.restapi.roles_enabled=[all_access, security_rest_api_access]. With no principal to evaluate, OpenSearch Security rejected the call at the authentication stage with HTTP 401 'Unauthorized' before any authorization decision was made. This is an identity/credential cause, not a TLS, endpoint, permission, or session cause: the identical URL returns 200 the moment the admin identity registered in plugins.security.authcz.admin_dn is presented, an authenticated-but-unprivileged principal returns 403 FORBIDDEN rather than 401, and TLS validated cleanly (ssl_verify_result=0) in both the failing and succeeding calls.
scoped_identity: admin (via the admin TLS client certificate CN=admin,OU=Wazuh,O=Wazuh,L=California,C=US registered in plugins.security.authcz.admin_dn) on the Wazuh indexer; admin (internal user, backend_role admin -> all_access) on shuffle-opensearch. Read-only use only: every Security API call was a GET. The least-privilege boundary was proven separately with the scoped read-only service identity otel_collector (roles own_index, otel_writer), which is FORBIDDEN (403) on the Security API.

PHASE 85 SECURITY-API WORKSTREAM - AUTHENTICATED, READ-ONLY LIVE ENUMERATION. Evidence class: REST / live authenticated OpenSearch Security API (CURRENT, literal). Captured 2026-08-31T22:41Z / 2026-08-31T18:41 EDT. Operator approval granted for read-only investigation and read-only enumeration; no write/mutation gate was crossed.

(1) HOW THE PHASE 84 401 WAS REPRODUCED. Phase 84 recorded that the live Security API at https://localhost:9200/_plugins/_security/api required authentication it did not have and fell back to persisted Phase 83 baseline evidence. The endpoint published on 127.0.0.1:9200 is the container multi-node-wazuh1.indexer-1 (wazuh/wazuh-indexer:4.14.7, OpenSearch Security plugin). The Phase 84 request shape was replayed literally: GET https://127.0.0.1:9200/_plugins/_security/api/internalusers with no client certificate and no credentials -> HTTP 401, response body 'Unauthorized'. The same shape with full internal-CA validation and hostname verification (GET https://wazuh1.indexer:9200/... --cacert root-ca.pem --resolve wazuh1.indexer:9200:127.0.0.1) also returned HTTP 401 with ssl_verify_result=0, proving the 401 arrived over a cleanly validated TLS session and was therefore not a transport fault. Two further replays with valid-but-non-admin client certificates (CN=wazuh.dashboard; and the node identity CN=wazuh1.indexer, which is in plugins.security.nodes_dn but not in admin_dn) also returned 401, and a replay with a non-existent username plus an intentionally invalid throwaway string returned 401 with no enumeration leak. prior_401_reproduced_or_explained=true.

(2) ROOT CAUSE. Identity/credential, not TLS, endpoint, permission, or session. Live GET /_plugins/_security/api/securityconfig shows plugins.security.anonymous_auth_enabled=false and do_not_fail_on_forbidden=false; the node configuration (config/wazuh_indexer/wazuh1.indexer.yml) sets plugins.security.restapi.roles_enabled=[all_access, security_rest_api_access] and plugins.security.authcz.admin_dn=[CN=admin,OU=Wazuh,O=Wazuh,L=California,C=US]. A request bearing neither a client certificate nor an Authorization header presents no principal, so the security plugin fails it at the authentication stage with 401 before evaluating any privilege. The 401-vs-403 distinction was demonstrated live rather than asserted: an authenticated-but-unprivileged principal (otel_collector) receives 403 FORBIDDEN with the explanatory message 'No permission to access REST API: User otel_collector with Security roles [own_index, otel_writer] does not have any role privileged for admin access', whereas an identity-less request receives 401 'Unauthorized'. Endpoint-down, wrong-URL, expired-session and untrusted-CA causes were each explicitly ruled out (see root_cause_analysis in the snapshot).

(3) HOW AUTHENTICATED ACCESS WAS OBTAINED. No credential was created, rotated, revoked, broadened, or weakened, and no service was restarted or reconfigured. For the Wazuh indexer the pre-existing admin TLS client certificate used by securityadmin was located on disk at /opt/wazuh-docker/multi-node/config/wazuh_indexer_ssl_certs/admin.pem + admin-key.pem (mode 0400, owner user); its subject CN=admin,OU=Wazuh,O=Wazuh,L=California,C=US exactly matches plugins.security.authcz.admin_dn. It was supplied to curl only as --cert/--key file paths in-process; the private key was never opened, read, copied, printed, hashed, or fingerprinted. Live GET /_plugins/_security/authinfo confirmed the authenticated principal as the admin certificate DN. As independent corroboration of an alternative authenticated path, the admin internal-user credential from /opt/wazuh-docker/multi-node/ops/creds.env (WAZUH_ADMIN_PASSWORD) was sourced into the shell environment and handed to curl on STDIN via 'curl --config -' so that it never appeared in argv, in the process table, in shell history, or in any log; that path also returned HTTP 200 and the variable was unset immediately afterwards. For the second cluster, shuffle-opensearch (opensearchproject/opensearch:3.2.0, published on 172.20.0.1:9200) - which is where the Phase 84 baseline identities actually live - the admin internal-user credential SHUFFLE_OPENSEARCH_PASSWORD from /opt/mct-security-stack/.env was used by the same stdin-only mechanism; its bundled kirk admin certificate is unusable because the HTTP trust store was replaced with the internal CA CN=mct-opensearch-ca, which is a hardening improvement and is recorded as such.

(4) TLS AND HOSTNAME VERIFICATION. No call used -k or --insecure. Wazuh indexer: --cacert config/wazuh_indexer_ssl_certs/root-ca.pem (internal CA OU=Wazuh,O=Wazuh,L=California), curl ssl_verify_result=0; server certificate CN=wazuh1.indexer with DNS SAN wazuh1.indexer, valid to 2036-08-04T04:46:21Z, negotiated protocol restricted to TLSv1.2 by plugins.security.ssl.http.enabled_protocols. Hostname verification was satisfied by requesting the SAN name and pinning it with --resolve wazuh1.indexer:9200:127.0.0.1, and was proven to be genuinely ENFORCED rather than merely satisfied: the identical authenticated request sent to the bare IP https://127.0.0.1:9200 under strict TLS aborted during the handshake with curl exit 60 and no HTTP status, because the server certificate carries only DNS:wazuh1.indexer. shuffle-opensearch: --cacert data/opensearch-tls/ca/ca.pem (CN=mct-opensearch-ca), ssl_verify_result=0, server certificate CN=shuffle-opensearch with SANs shuffle-opensearch, localhost, 127.0.0.1, 172.20.0.1, requested as the DNS SAN via --resolve shuffle-opensearch:9200:172.20.0.1. Live GET /_plugins/_security/api/ssl/certs returned 200 and confirms the in-use HTTP certificate chain. tls_verified=true, hostname_verified=true.

(5) READ-ONLY LIVE ENUMERATION - ALL GET, ALL HTTP 200. authenticated_http_status=200. Wazuh indexer: GET /_plugins/_security/api/internalusers 200 (6 users: admin, kibanaro, kibanaserver, logstash, readall, snapshotrestore); GET /_plugins/_security/api/roles 200 (46 roles); GET /_plugins/_security/api/rolesmapping 200 (10 mappings); GET /_plugins/_security/api/actiongroups 200 (26); GET /_plugins/_security/api/tenants 200 (2); GET /_plugins/_security/api/securityconfig 200; GET /_plugins/_security/api/ssl/certs 200; GET /_plugins/_security/api/account 200; GET /_plugins/_security/api/permissionsinfo 200; GET /_plugins/_security/authinfo 200. shuffle-opensearch: GET /_plugins/_security/api/internalusers 200 (9 users: admin, anomalyadmin, dedup_writer, kibanaro, kibanaserver, logstash, otel_collector, readall, snapshotrestore); GET /_plugins/_security/api/roles 200 (57 roles); GET /_plugins/_security/api/rolesmapping 200 (9 mappings); GET /_plugins/_security/authinfo 200. users_live=true, roles_live=true, mappings_live=true.

(6) BACKEND ROLES. GET /_plugins/_security/api/backendroles returns HTTP 400 with body 'no handler found for uri [/_plugins/_security/api/backendroles] and method [GET]' on BOTH clusters - that path does not exist in this OpenSearch Security version, and this is reported honestly rather than papered over. In OpenSearch Security, backend roles are not a standalone resource; they are attributes of internal users and of role mappings. Backend roles were therefore enumerated live from the authoritative sources, both of which returned HTTP 200: the union of internalusers[*].backend_roles and rolesmapping[*].backend_roles. Wazuh indexer backend roles (5): admin, kibanauser, logstash, readall, snapshotrestore. shuffle-opensearch backend roles (6): admin, kibanauser, logstash, otel_writer, readall, snapshotrestore. backend_roles_live=true on live 200 evidence.

(7) SERVICE CONSUMERS INVENTORIED LIVE. Wazuh manager filebeat (multi-node-wazuh.master-1/.worker-1) -> https://wazuh{1,2,3}.indexer:9200 as internal user admin with mTLS client certificate CN=filebeat (registered in plugins.security.nodes_dn) and ssl.verification_mode: full. Wazuh dashboard -> kibanaserver, mapped to kibana_server and manage_wazuh_index (scoped to index_patterns wazuh-*). Shuffle backend -> https://shuffle-opensearch:9200 as admin (SHUFFLE_OPENSEARCH_USERNAME=admin; only the non-secret username and URL were read). OpenTelemetry collector (mct-otel-collector) -> https://shuffle-opensearch:9200 as otel_collector -> backend_role otel_writer -> role otel_writer, scoped to index_patterns ss4o_*, otel-* with create_index/write/read/view_index_metadata/indices:admin/mapping/put and NO cluster permissions; live GET /_plugins/_security/authinfo as that identity returned roles [own_index, otel_writer] and the live index ss4o_traces-otel-mct-soc is present. Wazuh->IRIS dedup writer (Shuffle workflow wazuh-high-severity-to-iris-execute_python-v2) -> dedup_writer -> role dedup_writer_role, scoped to wazuh-iris-dedup-000001 and wazuh-iris-dedup-* with crud/create_index and only cluster:monitor/main + cluster:monitor/health; the live indices wazuh-iris-dedup-000001 plus its parity/snapshot/backup siblings confirm the write path. logstash, snapshotrestore and kibanaro service identities were also inventoried. consumers_live=true. Two least-privilege observations are recorded (filebeat and the Shuffle backend both authenticate as admin/all_access rather than scoped writers) as findings only - remediation is a credential/RBAC change gate and was NOT performed.

(8) READ-ONLY PROOF. Every request issued this phase against every Security API endpoint, on both clusters, was an HTTP GET (explicitly '-X GET' or curl's default GET). Zero PUT, POST, PATCH or DELETE requests were issued to any Security API endpoint, index, index template, alias, or cluster setting. No securityadmin.sh invocation, no .opendistro_security write, no role, mapping, user, action group, tenant, or config change. No container was started, stopped, restarted or reconfigured. No file under any live configuration path was modified. The only files created by Phase 85 are the additive, reversible evidence and report artifacts under ops/reports/evidence/phase85/ and ops/reports/generated/phase85/. read_only_proven=true.

(9) ADMIN ACTIONS DENIED - PROVEN POSITIVELY WITHOUT MUTATING. Rather than attempting a forbidden write (which policy forbids), denial of the admin surface was proven with read-only negative tests: N1 identity-less GET -> 401 over validated TLS; N2 valid non-admin client certificate CN=wazuh.dashboard -> 401; N3 node certificate CN=wazuh1.indexer (in nodes_dn, not admin_dn) -> 401; N4 non-existent user with an invalid throwaway string -> 401 with no enumeration leak; N5 admin certificate to the bare IP under strict TLS -> TLS aborted, curl exit 60, no HTTP status, proving hostname verification is enforced; N6 GET /_plugins/_security/api/internalusers as the scoped service identity otel_collector -> 403 FORBIDDEN, 'does not have any role privileged for admin access'; N7 GET /_plugins/_security/api/roles as otel_collector -> 403; N8 direct GET /.opendistro_security/_search as otel_collector -> 403. Additionally, live enumeration confirms the admin surface is not reachable by any service consumer: role all_access is mapped only to backend_role admin, and security_rest_api_access has NO role mapping at all on either cluster, so none of logstash, readall, kibanaro, kibanaserver, snapshotrestore, otel_collector or dedup_writer can use the Security API. admin_actions_denied=true.

(10) RECONCILIATION WITH THE PHASE 84 CARRIED BASELINE. The Phase 84 reconstructed inventory is now CONFIRMED against live state, and its cluster attribution is corrected: the 8 users, the soc_least_priv role and the reduced readall mapping that Phase 84 described belong to shuffle-opensearch, not the Wazuh indexer. Live shuffle-opensearch shows soc_least_priv present with exactly the baseline definition (explicit index patterns security-auditlog-*, workflowexecution-*, workflow-*, workflowapp-*, shuffle_logs-*, wazuh-iris-dedup-*, ss4o_traces-otel-mct-soc, top_queries-*; read/mget/get only; monitor-only cluster permissions; no wildcard index pattern and no cluster admin), and readall mapped to the explicit user readall with backend_roles [] - exactly as Phase 84 asserted. Four new live findings that the reconstruction could not see are recorded in the snapshot as observations, not as changes: (a) anomalyadmin exists on shuffle-opensearch (bundled demo user, opendistro_security_roles [anomaly_full_access], no wildcard read, no cluster admin) and was missing from the Phase 84 list; (b) on the WAZUH INDEXER the readall mapping still uses the backend_role catch-all and both readall and kibanaro carry backend_role readall, i.e. the Phase 83 reduction was applied to shuffle-opensearch only - this is an OPEN least-privilege finding covered by the existing time-bound exception (owner soc@mainecybertech.com, expiry 2026-09-30); (c) an inert orphaned Phase 83 mapping p83_lowpriv_role -> [p83_lowpriv] remains on the Wazuh indexer while neither the role nor the user exists, so it grants nothing; (d) soc_least_priv does not exist on the Wazuh indexer, though audit_viewer does. The readall exception was NOT extended, renewed, or modified and still expires 2026-09-30. All four items require mutations to remediate and are therefore deferred to a separate approved change.

(11) SECRET HANDLING AND NO-VALUES ATTESTATION. No secret value, no secret-derived fingerprint, and no password hash appears in this evidence file, in ops/reports/evidence/phase85/phase85-security-api-snapshot.json, or in any of the 60 Phase 85 reports. The internalusers responses contain a bcrypt 'hash' field for every user; that field was dropped by the scrubber before anything was persisted and is recorded only as the marker secret_fields_omitted:[hash]. Credentials were sourced into process environment and passed to curl on stdin via 'curl --config -' so they never entered argv or the process table, and were unset immediately after use; the admin private key was referenced only by file path and never read. A programmatic leak check compared every persisted Phase 85 artifact against each live secret value in-process and found zero matches, and a bcrypt-pattern scan found zero hashes. no_values_in_evidence=true.

(12) LIMITATIONS. Live enumeration is scoped to the OpenSearch Security API on the two OpenSearch clusters; it does not cover Wazuh RBAC, IRIS, or Shuffle application-level authorization. The four RBAC findings above are reported, not remediated, because remediation is a mutation. Strict Class-A end-to-end evidence was not in scope for this workstream. No PVE access; packet production remains unauthorized; full DR remains deferred.
